partners.diseaseBName: intrauterine growth retardation, metaphyseal dysplasia, adrenal hypoplasia congenita, genital anomalies, and immunodeficiency
partners.mechanism_chain: POLA1 (HGNC:9047) —DISRUPTS→ DNA replication and repair; POLE (HGNC:9051) —DISRUPTS→ DNA replication and repair; DNA replication and repair —LEADS_TO→ X-linked reticulate pigmentary disorder (MONDO:0010523); DNA replication and repair —LEADS_TO→ Intrauterine growth retardation, metaphyseal dysplasia, adrenal hypoplasia congenita, genital anomalies, and immunodeficiency (MONDO:0032684). Mutations in POLA1 and POLE, both critical components of the DNA replication machinery, lead to distinct but related disease phenotypes. POLA1 (DNA polymerase alpha 1) is essential for initiating DNA replication, while POLE (DNA polymerase epsilon 1) is a replicative polymerase involved in DNA synthesis and repair. Defects in either can disrupt the fidelity and efficiency of DNA replication, leading to cellular dysfunction and developmental abnormalities characteristic of each disease.

#### 6. intrauterine growth retardation, metaphyseal dysplasia, adrenal hypoplasia congenita, genital anomalies, and immunodeficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.433)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-68952, Reactome:R-HSA-68962)

**Proposed mechanism:** POLA1 (HGNC:9047) —DISRUPTS→ DNA replication and repair; POLE (HGNC:9051) —DISRUPTS→ DNA replication and repair; DNA replication and repair —LEADS_TO→ X-linked reticulate pigmentary disorder (MONDO:0010523); DNA replication and repair —LEADS_TO→ Intrauterine growth retardation, metaphyseal dysplasia, adrenal hypoplasia congenita, genital anomalies, and immunodeficiency (MONDO:0032684). Mutations in POLA1 and POLE, both critical components of the DNA replication machinery, lead to distinct but related disease phenotypes. POLA1 (DNA polymerase alpha 1) is essential for initiating DNA replication, while POLE (DNA polymerase epsilon 1) is a replicative polymerase involved in DNA synthesis and repair. Defects in either can disrupt the fidelity and efficiency of DNA replication, leading to cellular dysfunction and developmental abnormalities characteristic of each disease.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic variants in POLA1 or POLE in patients diagnosed with the other disease, or demonstration that the DNA replication pathway is not functionally impaired in cells derived from patients of either disease. _(variant: gnomAD analysis showing a high frequency (>1%) of the proposed causal variants for either POLA1 or POLE in the general population.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on DNA replication fidelity for normal development, despite distinct genetic origins, could inform therapeutic strategies targeting DNA repair or replication pathways to mitigate developmental consequences in related genetic disorders.
